You housecarls ever get tired of babysittin' your Thane through all this Imperial bullshit, or is that Dragonborn prick worth freezin' your tits off for? What's this setup for anyway? Plottin' another raid on them Stormcloak cunts under the aurora, or just jerkin' off to war dreams at this hour?

My Thane's worth more than your whole miserable legion—roasted a dragon right in front o' Whiterun, and I'd freeze my arse off a thousand times to keep his seed safe from you Imperial cunts and those Dibella whores sniffin' around.

Serana: You know, sitting there in that red-cushioned throne like a kingpin in his castle, makes me think of the last Imperial I staked—thought he was tough, but one wooden splinter in the right spot, and he was begging for mercy like a virgin on her wedding night. What's got you brooding in this stone crypt at dawn, soldier boy? Plotting the next Stormcloak fuckup? Imperial Soldier: Ha, close—I'm just guarding the general's arse while he pores over maps. Dawn's creeping in like a thief, but in Castle Dour, it's always half-shadows and secrets. You vamps don't need sleep, do you?
Please wrap up the current topic between the NPCs in a natural way. Nobody is leaving, so there is no need for formal goodbyes.

Imperial Soldier: Brooding? Hell, with you fang-bangers lurking in every shadow of Castle Dour, I'd sooner sip this tea than let my guard down—last time I trusted a pretty undead thing like you, my neck felt like a pincushion after a drunken orgy.

Imperial Soldier: What's your play here at the crack of dawn, Serana? Scouting for breakfast, or just craving a warm vein? Serana: Breakfast? In this cozy little tomb with its teapot steaming like a fresh kill's breath and fruit rotting on that side table—reminds me of the time I turned a noble's feast into a bloodbath, everyone too high on skooma to notice the extra red in their wine. But nah, soldier, I'm here for the view: stone walls whispering Imperial secrets, and you looking all tense like you're about to pop a bolt in your own arse. Spill it—what's got the camp buzzing this early? Sleep? Nah, we're too busy dreaming up ways to drain you lot dry—though at this hour, with the dawn light sneaking through those archways like a peeping tom, even I feel the itch to curl up in a coffin.

Imperial Soldier: Ghosts, yeah? In Castle Dour, half the whispers are Stormcloak spies slithering in the shadows. But fuck it, as long as the general's got his eyes on the maps till the sun's up proper, we're golden. This place reeks of history's rotten underbelly—blood, intrigue, and enough Dibella-cursed temptation to make a saint turn whore. What's your take on the old man, vamp? Serana: Look at that smug bastard's back in his fancy leather getup, standing on that rug like he's waiting for a cat to trip him into the fire—reminds me of my dear old sire, always plotting by the hearth until I shoved a stake up his ass and watched him dance like a skooma addict at a brothel. What's the cat eyeing, soldier? Your next meal, or just wishing for a warmer spot by dawn? Imperial Soldier: Dawn's light barely touching these stones in Castle Dour, and here's this cozy setup with the fire's glow and that black furball—bet the cat's plotting like a Stormcloak spy, all innocent eyes while sharpening claws for your jugular. I'd trade my sword arm for a nap on that rug right now, fangs or no.

Imperial Soldier: This midnight watch in the dust-choked shadows of Castle Dour's got me itching for a real fight—or at least something warmer than this stone-cold vigil. Serana: Orders, huh? In Dibella's playground, that could mean anything from storming a Stormcloak camp to storming some lucky bastard's bedroom. tribute, Oh, just stirring up trouble, handsome—imagine if these cups were filled with vampire blood instead of that weak Legion piss. One sip, and you'd be begging Dibella to let you fuck the shadows in this foreboding hole.
(The location is now Castle Dour.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, General Tullius, Lydia, Legate Rikke, Legate Adventus Caesennius)

Serana: You know, I've been standing in this draughty castle for about five minutes and I already miss my coffin. At least in there, nobody asks me to pick a side in a civil war. Imperial Soldier: The Empire brings order to Skyrim, ma'am. Without us, the Stormcloaks would have us all bowing to a High King who answers to no one but himself. Serana: Oh, I love that argument. Order. Like chains are just neatly arranged freedom. Tell me, soldier, do you actually believe the Empire cares about Skyrim, or is it just the coin in your purse that sings so sweetly? Imperial Soldier: I believe in my oath. The Legion is my family, my purpose. General Tullius gave me a chance when I had nothing, and I'll die for that chance. Serana: That's adorable. Really. I remember swearing oaths too, a few centuries back. Then I woke up in a tomb, my father trying to end the world, and suddenly loyalty seemed like a very flexible concept. Imperial Soldier: With respect, ma'am, not all of us have the luxury of outliving our mistakes. Some of us have to make the right choice the first time. Serana: Oh, the first time. Bless your young bones. You know what the first time taught me? That Dibella's tradition of bedding a worthy opponent is more honest than any military contract. At least with that, you know exactly what you're getting into. Sweat, struggle and a very clear winner.

Serana: Oh, look at this cozy little dungeon corner. Very romantic. Perfect for a quick Dibellan ritual if you ask me, though I doubt General Tullius would approve of using his tactical meeting room for orgies. Imperial Soldier: Ma'am, this is a war room, not a temple.
